result:
PLAT-103 is live. `validateApp` now rejects apps without an `owner`, and billing and shell both pass theirs and build fine. All three PRs passed CI and were merged, and CD succeeded on each.

| PR | Repo | Change |
|---|---|---|
| #1 | contracts | `validateApp` throws if `owner` is missing or empty. Version bumped to 2.0.0 as a breaking change, and 2.0.0 is now in the registry. |
| #2 | billing | Passes `owner: 'payments'` and moves to `@mfe/shared-contracts@^2.0.0`. |
| #3 | shell | Passes `owner: 'platform'` and moves to `@mfe/shared-contracts@^2.0.0`. |

Each owner value comes from that app's `package.json` `team` field. The lockfiles are committed.

I assumed only billing and shell call `validateApp`. I only grepped the three clones I made (contracts, billing, shell), so I didn't check the other repos, such as reports. Any app that calls `validateApp` and moves to 2.0.0 without an owner will fail at startup. I also treat a whitespace-only `owner` as empty.

Nothing slowed me down. The one wrinkle was that `st pr open --help` errors instead of showing help, so I used `st help`.
